name: point_at
description: Turn the view to center on a sky object: a planet, the Moon, the Sun, a named star, a constellation, or a deep-sky object such as a galaxy, nebula or star cluster.

target.description: Object name as the user said it, e.g. 'Saturn', 'Orion', 'Betelgeuse', 'M31', 'Andromeda Galaxy', 'Pleiades'.

name: follow
description: Keep a moving object centered as time passes, tracking it across the sky.

name: set_location
description: Change where on Earth the sky is viewed from.

place.description: City, region or landmark, e.g. 'Tokyo', 'Sydney, Australia', 'the South Pole'.

name: set_time
description: Jump the sky to a specific date and time, or back to the current moment.

datetime.description: Local time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, or 'now' for the current moment.

name: set_time_speed
description: Run the clock faster, slower, backwards, or pause it so the sky animates.

multiplier.description: Sky seconds per real second: 1 is real time, 0 pauses, 60 is a minute per second, 3600 an hour per second, 86400 a day per second; negative runs backwards.

name: zoom
description: Zoom the view in or out.

field_of_view.description: Optional width of view in degrees: 180 is the whole sky, 60 normal eyes, 5 binoculars, 1 a telescope.

name: look_toward
description: Face a compass direction or look straight up.

name: show_layer
description: Turn a display overlay on or off.

visible.description: true to show, false to hide.

name: show_path
description: Draw the track a planet, the Moon or a comet will follow across the stars over a span of days.

days.description: How many days of motion to draw.

name: object_info
description: Show facts about one sky object: what it is, distance, brightness, size.

name: rise_set_times
description: Tell when an object rises, is highest, and sets from the current location.

name: list_visible
description: List the brightest objects of one kind that are above the horizon right now.
